answer: A staked-identity registry holds each identity's deposit in a shared vault contract, and every onboarding attestation escrows part of the sponsor's stake behind the new account. If a cluster proves a fable and shares one controller, all its deposits are slashed together. That kills the marble trick of spinning thousands of cheap sockpuppets: the attacker must fund every identity at full stake, so cost scales linearly and matches honest participation. Rewards vest only after a cooling epoch, keeping capital locked and exposed, and per-cluster caps make extra accounts earn nothing.
